**Trader sentiment heavily favors an 88–89°F peak at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (KDFW) on June 16, 2026, with that bin at 75.5% implied probability.** Official National Weather Service guidance and supporting model runs converge on a daily high in the upper 80s amid partly to mostly cloudy skies, scattered afternoon showers or thunderstorms (20–30% coverage), and moderate northeast to east winds that limit full solar heating. 

Seasonal climatology for mid-June points to highs near 92–94°F, but elevated dew points and convective activity are suppressing afternoon temperatures by several degrees relative to clear-sky expectations. Current observations show readings climbing through the mid-80s by midday, consistent with forecasts of a peak near 88–90°F. The modest 19.5% odds on 90–91°F reflect limited upside risk if skies clear more than expected late in the day, while higher bins remain negligible given the moisture and cloud trends. Resolution depends on the precise maximum at the official KDFW station, with any stronger insolation or delayed convection as the main variables that could shift the outcome.

A few showers are expected but unlikely to alter the peak temperature materially. Seasonal outlooks from NIWA indicate near-average conditions overall for the region, providing climatological context that reinforces why traders have concentrated probability on 14–15°C rather than extremes. Updated model runs and any MetService revisions in the final 12–24 hours before resolution remain the key variables that could shift these market-implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models place Kuala Lumpur’s June 17 maximum near the long-term June average of 32 °C.** Multiple guidance sources, including AccuWeather’s month-ahead outlook and shorter-range runs, show daily highs centered on 30–33 °C, with the single most likely 24-hour maximum falling in the 31–32 °C range. This distribution directly explains why those two buckets currently command the largest market shares.

**Tropical thermodynamics and local steering patterns keep extremes unlikely.** Persistent southwesterly flow, typical of the southwest monsoon transition, limits strong subsidence that would otherwise produce hotter afternoons. Scattered afternoon thunderstorms, already indicated in the latest official guidance, are expected to cap peak temperatures through evaporative cooling and increased cloud cover. Historical June maxima rarely exceed 34 °C without a pronounced ridge, which is absent in current analyses.

**No recent anomalies have shifted the outlook.** Observations through mid-June show temperatures running close to climatology, with no pronounced heat spell or unusual moisture surge. Ensemble spread remains modest, keeping the 30–33 °C window dominant. Updated model runs tonight and tomorrow morning will provide the final confirmation before resolution.

**Trader sentiment for Cape Town’s June 17 maximum temperature centers on the South African Weather Service (SAWS) outlook for partly cloudy and cold-to-cool conditions with isolated coastal showers.** This aligns with June’s climatological average high of 17–18 °C (rarely exceeding 22 °C), positioning 19–21 °C as plausible outcomes while keeping higher values low-probability.

Key drivers include the passage of a recent cold front and a coastal low that maintain onshore flow and cloud cover, limiting daytime heating. SAWS explicitly describes “cold to cool” conditions for 17–18 June, consistent with post-frontal stabilization and modest insolation under partial cloud. Historical analogs and ensemble spread show typical June maxima clustered near 17 °C, with 20 °C requiring either clearer skies or a brief berg-wind influence that current guidance does not strongly support.

Market-implied odds (20 °C at 40.5 %, 19 °C at 26.5 %, 21 °C at 15.5 %) therefore reflect residual uncertainty in the precise timing of any clearing or local station micro-variations at Cape Town International Airport rather than a strong signal for above-average warmth. New SAWS or global model updates over the next 12–24 hours will likely tighten the distribution around the cooler end of the current range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Austin's June 17 high temperature centers on the low-to-mid 90s°F, with 92-93°F leading at 39.5% implied probability, followed by 90-91°F (25.5%) and 94-95°F (22.5%).** These probabilities reflect the tight clustering of National Weather Service and model guidance around Austin-Bergstrom climatological normals for mid-June, where the average daily high is approximately 93°F.

Key scientific drivers include persistent subtropical high pressure supporting daytime heating to near-seasonal levels, combined with moderate Gulf moisture that limits extreme warming while increasing the chance of afternoon cumulus build-up or isolated thunderstorms. Such convection can cap maximum temperatures a degree or two below guidance if it develops earlier than expected. Recent NWS point forecasts and ensemble runs have shown minimal day-to-day shifts, keeping the distribution narrow and centered near 92-94°F. Historical analogs from similar synoptic patterns confirm that deviations beyond 96°F or below 89°F are uncommon without a stronger frontal passage or clear-air subsidence, both of which are not indicated in current data. The market's heavy weighting on the 90-95°F range thus mirrors the high-confidence consensus from official forecast agencies for a near-normal summer day.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from regional models and agencies like the Pakistan Meteorological Department point to a June 18 peak near 34°C in Karachi, driven by typical pre-monsoon southwesterly winds and Arabian Sea marine influence that enhance humidity near 70-80% and moderate daytime heating. This aligns with climatological baselines of 33-36°C highs for mid-June. Trader consensus clusters on 34°C and 35°C because small differences in sea-breeze timing, cloud cover, or wind strength can shift the maximum by 1°C, while stronger suppression of marine air or clearer skies could briefly allow 36°C. Updated model runs and real-time observations in the next 48 hours will refine resolution criteria for the daily high.
